neighbours.label: the word after a totality intensifier that marks absence or difference: 'complete lack', 'total absence', 'completely different'
fire: The report criticized the complete lack of oversight at the agency.
Patients with this condition show a total absence of pain responses.
After the update, the app looked completely different from before.
There was a total lack of communication between the two teams.
The village suffered from a complete absence of clean water.
Her second novel took an entirely different approach to the story.
His speech revealed a complete lack of understanding of the issue.
The two samples produced totally different results in the lab.
quiet: The report criticized the weak oversight at the agency.
Patients with this condition show a reduced response to pain.
After the update, the app looked slightly cleaner than before.
There was some communication between the two teams.
The village suffered from a shortage of clean water.
Her second novel took a similar approach to the story.
His speech revealed a deep understanding of the issue.
The two samples produced nearly identical results in the lab.

notes: Card: ' lack' x6, ' altogether' x5, ' absence', ' different', after complete/total. Opposite pole is the positive side of the same scale: 'full force', 'full extent', 'full range'. Near misses keep the nouns' topics with partial or no totality.
